//: Client-side routing. The app is a single-page bundle: React Router owns
every path, but the server has only ever been given index.html. A visitor
landing straight on /about — from a link, a bookmark or a search result —
asked Vercel for a file that does not exist and got a 404. Only / worked,
because only / is a real file.
The rewrite hands index.html to any path so the router can resolve it in
the browser. It is a rewrite and not a redirect on purpose: the URL must
stay as typed, or the router would have nothing left to route on.
api/ is excluded explicitly. Vercel resolves functions in its filesystem
phase, before rewrites, so a bare catch-all would work today — but that is
a detail of phase ordering, and the inquiry endpoint quietly answering
with the HTML page instead of sending an email is not a failure anyone
would enjoy diagnosing. Saying it outright costs nothing.
